summary: Timeboxed, minimal customer-scope snapshot for GDPR scope validation (prod traces + redaction plan)
description:
Issue summary: Legal has requested a narrowly-scoped, timeboxed snapshot of production request traces and delivery logs to validate the scope of a GDPR subject access assessment. The snapshot must include only sessions matching the provided customer identifiers and must be redacted according to the approved pattern before any human reviews.

Requested by: Internal Legal (S. Kline) on 2026-03-11.
Justification: Confirm whether retained logs include personally identifiable information for a specific data subject and validate our redaction heuristics.
Required deliveries: (1) A minimized, schema-documented tarball containing redacted request/response snippets (max 200 sessions), delivery logs, and request metadata; (2) a redaction report listing the patterns applied and false-positive/negative risk notes; (3) ephemeral, auditable access for two Legal reviewers for 72 hours.
Constraints: No broad full-table exports, no unrestricted access to raw payloads, all artifacts must be scanned with the automated redaction tool and reviewed by Privacy before release.
impact: Potential regulatory exposure if raw PII is disclosed — must provide evidence quickly to avoid escalation. Operational impact: moderate; Data-ops and SRE timeboxed effort required (estimated 6-8 person-hours).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Identify customer identifiers from Legal (provided list). 2) Run targeted trace query against prod trace-index with strict filters (session_id IN list AND timestamp range). 3) Pipe results through automated redaction script. 4) Manual review by Privacy on a 10% sample. 5) Package artifacts and create audited download with sponsorship ticket. 6) Revoke access after 72h and record audit entries.
logs: Query executed against prod-traces-2026.* index (eu-west) with query id q-20260312-9f3. Initial hit-count: 187 sessions. Raw sample (first 2 entries) copied to secure temp for redaction step. Audit token: audit-INT-523678-03. System logs show spike in trace retrieval at 2026-03-12T14:12:02Z and successful completion at 2026-03-12T15:04:27Z. No 5xx errors observed.
investigation_notes:
- Initial search returned 187 session records, matching Legal-provided identifiers.
- Automated redaction removed ISO timestamps and masked potential email shapes and free-text PII tokens by default.
- Privacy ran a manual review on 19 samples (10%). Found 1 case where a long-form user message contained an unmasked credit-card-like sequence; redaction regex updated to cover that pattern.
- SRE validated retrieval pipeline and confirmed query did not touch cold storage buckets.
- Data-ops confirmed export size 45MB compressed.
- Security approved ephemeral storage location and scoped IAM role (role: data-extract-timebox-523678) with least privilege.
- Access window requested: 72 hours; access-provisioned at 2026-03-13T09:00Z.
resolution:
Provided a minimized, redacted snapshot to Legal via an expiring, auditable S3 presigned link and a separate redaction report. Updated redaction regex to catch additional numeric sequences resembling payment instruments. Access revoked automatically at 2026-03-16T09:05Z. All actions recorded in audit logs (audit-INT-523678-03). Follow-up: add the new regex to the central redaction ruleset and schedule a runbook update.
Workaround/fix: Implemented temporary patch to redaction script and ran an additional pass over the exported artifacts. Legal confirmed receipt and that artifacts were sufficient for scope validation.
Follow-up actions: (1) CR to add regex to redaction service (PR linked above), (2) update runbook to require 20% manual review for similar requests, (3) telemetry alert to flag remaining unmatched numeric sequences.
